title: Superpolynomial \(\mathrm{AC}^{0}[p]\)-Frege lower bounds
formal: For every fixed prime p, does there exist a family of propositional tautologies \((\tau _{p,n})_{n\ge 1}\), constructible in time polynomial in n, whose encoded lengths lie between n and \(n^{O}(1)\), such that each \(\tau _{p,n}\) is a DNF and, for every fixed proof-line depth d and every constant \(r>0\), infinitely many n have the following property: every depth-at-most-d Frege proof with \(MOD_{p}\) connectives of \(\tau _{p,n}\) has total encoded size greater than \(n^{r}\)? The proof system and depth convention are specified below; the family may depend on p but not on d or r.
definitions: A tautology evaluates to true on every Boolean assignment. A DNF is a disjunction of conjunctions of literals, with a literal being a variable or its negation. Fix a conventional sound, implicationally complete finite Frege calculus F over constants 0,1 and connectives NOT, AND, OR. A proof is a sequence of formulas, each a substitution instance of an axiom or obtained from earlier lines by a rule of F; earlier lines may be reused arbitrarily. Extend the language and rules as F(\(MOD_{p}\)) in Krajíček §\(5: MOD_{p,j}(A_{1},\ldots ,A_{t})\) is true precisely when the number of true arguments is j modulo p, for \(0\le j<p\). Besides F’s rules with formulas from this language, permit the empty-list axioms \(MOD_{p,0}\)() and \(\mathrm{NOT} MOD_{p,j}\)() for \(j\ne 0\), and all instances of \(MOD_{p,j}(\Gamma ,A) \leftrightarrow\) [(\(MOD_{p,j}(\Gamma ) \mathrm{AND} \mathrm{NOT} A\)) OR (\(MOD_{p,j- 1}(\Gamma ) \mathrm{AND} A\))], with \(j- 1\) taken modulo p and \(\Gamma\) any list of formulas. Constants and variables have depth zero; NOT and MOD increase depth by one, while consecutive ANDs, or consecutive ORs, are flattened and together count as one layer. Every line, including instantiated axioms, obeys the bound d. Proof size counts all symbols and encoded variable indices across all lines, together with rule annotations. Proofs are ordinary Frege proofs, without extension-variable definition axioms; they need not be tree-like or have bounded derivation-graph depth. Standard choices of F give equivalent systems up to polynomial overhead and a constant depth adjustment, immaterial when every fixed d is quantified.
answer_criterion: Exhibit the uniform tautology families and prove the stated superpolynomial proof-size lower bounds, or refute their existence. The tautology condition must itself be established: a formula that has no short proof because it is false is not a hard tautology. A lower bound only for bounded derivation depth, regular proofs, a restricted algebraic subsystem or Boolean circuits alone does not settle this question. A result for one prime is a major partial answer; this single card groups the full fixed-prime frontier rather than duplicating it for each modulus.
why: A central frontier in propositional proof complexity: current methods can handle ordinary bounded-depth reasoning but still cannot establish explicit superpolynomial lower bounds once modular counting is available. The problem tests how circuit lower-bound ideas can constrain entire deductions.

importance.reason: A classical next step beyond the strongest broadly established bounded-depth Frege lower bounds, with direct connections to algebraic proof systems and a persistent gap between circuit and proof complexity.

progress.text: Ajtai establishes superpolynomial bounded-depth Frege lower bounds for the pigeonhole principle; Pitassi, Beame and Impagliazzo’s 1993 paper gives exponential improvements. These systems lack \(MOD_{p}\) gates.
Krajíček develops extended Nullstellensatz systems and explains their connection to modular Frege lower bounds; §5 fixes the proof-system presentation used here.
Efremenko and Itsykson publish amortized-closure lifting and stronger size-versus-derivation-depth results for resolution over parities.
Lu, Santhanam and Tzameret publish their no-short-proof result for candidate DNFs, first posted in September 2025; unconditional tautologicity remains open.
Itsykson, Podolskii and Shekhovtsov give near-quadratic-depth lifting and a quadratic unconditional size lower bound for parity resolution. These do not settle general modular Frege.
Hakoniemi, Limaye and Tzameret release hard CNF instances for the read-once-oblivious algebraic-branching-program fragment of IPS.

status_note: Checked through 10 September 2026. The 2026 primary sources retain modular Frege lower bounds as open. ITCS 2026.99 does not prove that its hard-to-prove candidates are tautologies. ECCC TR26-018 restricts derivation depth or proves a polynomial size bound; TR26-070 treats a restricted algebraic certificate representation. None establishes the fully specified tautology families and unrestricted derivation size lower bounds requested here.

context_blocks.text: Proof complexity measures how long a formal explanation of a tautology must be. A short conclusion can require a much longer sequence of intermediate deductions. Restricting the depth of each intermediate formula limits the expressive power of individual statements while still allowing a long derivation and arbitrary reuse of earlier facts. Modular gates add compact statements about counts modulo p, such as parity when \(p=2\). Krajíček gives the explicit modular axiom presentation used in this card.

The corresponding problem without modular gates has been solved. Ajtai’s work gives superpolynomial lower bounds for the pigeonhole principle in bounded-depth Frege, and Pitassi, Beame and Impagliazzo strengthen these to exponential bounds. Their argument uses restrictions adapted to the combinatorics of partial matchings. Permitting modular counting defeats the direct extension of that approach: a short parity statement can remain meaningful after many ordinary variables have been fixed.

Circuit complexity provides an analogy but not a solution. Razborov and Smolensky establish lower bounds for constant-depth Boolean circuits with prime modular gates. A proof, however, is a sequence of related formulas, and every tautology itself computes the constant true function. Showing that some nonconstant function requires a large circuit therefore does not directly force long proofs of tautologies. The February 2026 work of Itsykson, Podolskii and Shekhovtsov explicitly identifies this remaining gap between circuit and proof lower bounds.

Resolution over parities is a much weaker subsystem whose lines are disjunctions of linear equations modulo two. Efremenko and Itsykson’s CCC 2025 work develops amortized closure and strengthens lifting lower bounds for restricted-depth parity-resolution refutations. The restriction there concerns the number of inference steps along a path in the derivation graph. That is different from the constant logical depth of each formula in \(\mathrm{AC}^{0}[p]\)-Frege. A long chain of shallow formulas remains allowed in the present question.

Itsykson, Podolskii and Shekhovtsov’s February 2026 lifting theorem gives derivation depth \(\Omega (w^{2}/\log  S)\) for size-S parity-resolution proofs when the underlying CNF needs resolution width w. It also gives a pure quadratic size lower bound. These are meaningful advances, but a quadratic bound is polynomial, and a tradeoff requiring sufficiently deep proofs still permits polynomial-size proofs with large derivation depth. Neither gives the superpolynomial unrestricted proof-size target here.

Lu, Santhanam and Tzameret’s ITCS 2026 result studies explicit DNF formulas expressing the difficulty of proving certain algebraic circuit lower bounds. They show that these formulas do not all have polynomial-size \(\mathrm{AC}^{0}[p]\)-Frege proofs. The unresolved point is whether the formulas are tautologies: the theorem leaves open the possibility that some are simply false. They provide a conditional route to tautologicity through hardness of proving properties related to tensor rank. This separates two obligations that a completed lower-bound construction must satisfy.

Algebraic proof systems offer another route, but their representation restrictions matter. Hakoniemi, Limaye and Tzameret’s May 2026 work gives hard CNF instances for a fragment of the Ideal Proof System represented by read-once oblivious algebraic branching programs. It overcomes the obstacle that earlier lower bounds in that line concerned purely algebraic, non-Boolean instances. It does not remove the restricted representation of certificates or establish lower bounds for full modular Frege.

The quantifiers exclude a fixed-degree lower bound such as \(n^{10}\) and require failure of every polynomial size bound at every fixed line depth. They also keep the target formulas short and efficiently constructible, so hardness cannot come from writing an exponentially large conclusion or searching indefinitely for an unnamed formula. Resolving this frontier would extend lower-bound methods to formal reasoning that can perform modular counting, an ability missing from ordinary bounded-depth Frege.

sentences: \(\mathrm{AC}^{0}[p]\)-Frege uses bounded-depth proof formulas that may include modular counting connectives for a fixed prime p.
The saved target asks for explicit polynomial-size DNF tautologies requiring superpolynomial proofs at every fixed formula depth.
Modular gates can retain counting information that ordinary restriction methods erase.
A lower bound would extend the reach of proof complexity beyond the established bounded-depth systems without modular counting.
The reviewed record distinguishes logical depth within proof lines from derivation depth and explains why circuit lower bounds do not automatically imply the requested proof lower bound.
